correctness.rationale: For positive weights, arbitrary complex phases are dominated by aligned positive phases. The substitution y_i=|x_i|^(p/2) converts the spatial numerical radius into a homogeneous positive maximization. A unique interior Perron maximizer and negative-definite tangent Hessian justify envelope differentiation at p=2, with correct factor 1/2. The 3-site sign calculation is exact. A tridiagonal characteristic identity and explicit Perron vector give small-b and large-b expansions with opposite signs for every a>c; no finite experiment is used to infer infinite limits. High-precision independent power-iteration sanity checks agree.

value.rationale: The precise numerical-radius response to moving away from Hilbert geometry is a natural operator-theoretic invariant. The theorem gives a universal computable spectral derivative, and proves a minimal four-coordinate phenomenon: altering an interior edge reverses the orientation response even with fixed strictly ordered outer weights. This is not an arbitrary numerical slice, and the crossover exists for every a>c; uniqueness and global p-dependence remain open.
